import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Conjecture 9.6

by V. A. Gorbunov

Is every independent basis of quasi-identities of a finite group finite?

*Reference:* [The Kourovka Notebook](https://arxiv.org/abs/1401.0300v46)
-/

namespace Kourovka.«9.6»

/-- A term in the first-order signature of groups, with variables indexed by
`ℕ`. -/
inductive GroupTerm where
  | var : ℕ → GroupTerm
  | one : GroupTerm
  | mul : GroupTerm → GroupTerm → GroupTerm
  | inv : GroupTerm → GroupTerm
  deriving DecidableEq

/-- The value of a group term under an assignment of its variables. -/
def GroupTerm.eval {G : Type*} [Group G] (v : ℕ → G) : GroupTerm → G
  | .var n => v n
  | .one => 1
  | .mul t u => t.eval v * u.eval v
  | .inv t => (t.eval v)⁻¹

/-- A quasi-identity in the group signature is a universally quantified
implication from a finite conjunction of equations to one equation. -/
structure GroupQuasiIdentity where
  premises : Finset (GroupTerm × GroupTerm)
  conclusion : GroupTerm × GroupTerm

/-- A group satisfies a quasi-identity if the implication holds under every
assignment of its variables. -/
def Satisfies {G : Type*} [Group G] (q : GroupQuasiIdentity) : Prop :=
  ∀ v : ℕ → G,
    (∀ e ∈ q.premises, e.1.eval v = e.2.eval v) →
      q.conclusion.1.eval v = q.conclusion.2.eval v

/-- A group satisfies a set of quasi-identities if it satisfies each member. -/
def SatisfiesSet {G : Type*} [Group G] (B : Set GroupQuasiIdentity) : Prop :=
  ∀ q ∈ B, Satisfies (G := G) q

/-- A set `B` is a basis for the quasi-identities of `G` if its models are
exactly the groups satisfying every quasi-identity satisfied by `G`. -/
def IsBasisFor (G : Type) [Group G] (B : Set GroupQuasiIdentity) : Prop :=
  ∀ (H : Type) [Group H],
    SatisfiesSet (G := H) B ↔
      ∀ q : GroupQuasiIdentity, Satisfies (G := G) q → Satisfies (G := H) q

/-- An independent basis is a basis no proper subset of which is still a
basis. -/
def IsIndependentBasisFor (G : Type) [Group G] (B : Set GroupQuasiIdentity) : Prop :=
  IsBasisFor G B ∧ ∀ C : Set GroupQuasiIdentity, C ⊂ B → ¬IsBasisFor G C

/--
Is it true that every independent basis of quasi-identities of every finite
group is finite? Here a basis axiomatizes the quasivariety generated by the
group, and independence means that no proper subset is also a basis.
-/
@[category research open, AMS 20]
theorem kourovka.«9.6» : answer(sorry) ↔
    ∀ (G : Type) [Group G] [Finite G] (B : Set GroupQuasiIdentity),
      IsIndependentBasisFor G B → B.Finite := by
  sorry

end Kourovka.«9.6»

Represented a quasi-identity as a universally quantified implication from a finite conjunction of group-term equations to one group-term equation; empty premise sets therefore include ordinary identities.
Defined a basis extensionally by its model class: its models are exactly the groups satisfying every quasi-identity true in G, i.e. the quasivariety generated by G.
Read “independent basis” as “irredundant basis” exactly as specified in the decomposition: no proper subset is still a basis.
Used `Finite G` for the finite-group hypothesis and `B.Finite` for finiteness of the given set of quasi-identities, preserving the distinction from existence of a finite basis.
As in nearby Kourovka files, groups and comparison models are quantified in Lean's small universe with `(G H : Type)`.

import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Conjecture 9.6

by V. A. Gorbunov

Is it true that an independent basis of quasiidentities of any finite group is finite?

A *quasi-identity* in the signature of groups is a universally closed formula
$$w_1(\bar x) = 1 \wedge \dots \wedge w_n(\bar x) = 1 \;\to\; w(\bar x) = 1,$$
where $n \geq 0$ and $w_1, \dots, w_n, w$ are group words (elements of the free group on the
variables $\bar x$). A set $B$ of quasi-identities is a *basis of quasi-identities* of a group $G$
if every member of $B$ holds in $G$ and every quasi-identity holding in $G$ is a consequence of
$B$; equivalently, a group satisfies $B$ if and only if it lies in the quasivariety generated
by $G$. The basis $B$ is *independent* if no member of $B$ is a consequence of the remaining
members (equivalently, no proper subset of $B$ is a basis).

*Reference:* [The Kourovka Notebook](https://arxiv.org/abs/1401.0300v46)
-/

namespace Kourovka.«9.6»

/-- A quasi-identity in the signature of groups, in the variables $x_0, x_1, \dots$ (indexed
by `ℕ`): the universally closed formula
$$w_1 = 1 \wedge \dots \wedge w_n = 1 \;\to\; w = 1$$
with finitely many premises $w_1, \dots, w_n$ and a conclusion $w$, all of which are group words,
i.e. elements of the free group `FreeGroup ℕ`. Identities are the case $n = 0$. -/
structure QuasiIdentity where
  /-- The premises $w_1, \dots, w_n$ of the quasi-identity. -/
  premises : Finset (FreeGroup ℕ)
  /-- The conclusion $w$ of the quasi-identity. -/
  conclusion : FreeGroup ℕ

namespace QuasiIdentity

/-- A group `H` satisfies the quasi-identity `q` if for every assignment of the variables in `H`
under which all premises of `q` evaluate to $1$, the conclusion of `q` evaluates to $1$. -/
def Holds (q : QuasiIdentity) (H : Type*) [Group H] : Prop :=
  ∀ f : ℕ → H, (∀ w ∈ q.premises, FreeGroup.lift f w = 1) →
    FreeGroup.lift f q.conclusion = 1

/-- A quasi-identity `q` is a consequence of a set `B` of quasi-identities if every group
satisfying all members of `B` satisfies `q`. -/
def IsConsequence (B : Set QuasiIdentity) (q : QuasiIdentity) : Prop :=
  ∀ (H : Type) [Group H], (∀ q' ∈ B, q'.Holds H) → q.Holds H

/-- A set `B` of quasi-identities is a basis of quasi-identities of the group `G` if every
member of `B` holds in `G` and every quasi-identity holding in `G` is a consequence of `B`. -/
def IsBasisOf (B : Set QuasiIdentity) (G : Type*) [Group G] : Prop :=
  (∀ q ∈ B, q.Holds G) ∧ ∀ q : QuasiIdentity, q.Holds G → IsConsequence B q

/-- A set `B` of quasi-identities is independent if no member of `B` is a consequence of the
remaining members of `B`. -/
def IsIndependent (B : Set QuasiIdentity) : Prop :=
  ∀ q ∈ B, ¬ IsConsequence (B \ {q}) q

/-- Every quasi-identity holds in a trivial group. -/
@[category API, AMS 8 20]
theorem holds_of_subsingleton (q : QuasiIdentity) (H : Type*) [Group H] [Subsingleton H] :
    q.Holds H :=
  fun _ _ => Subsingleton.elim _ _

/-- A quasi-identity whose conclusion is one of its premises holds in every group. -/
@[category API, AMS 8 20]
theorem holds_of_conclusion_mem (q : QuasiIdentity) (H : Type*) [Group H]
    (h : q.conclusion ∈ q.premises) : q.Holds H :=
  fun _ hf => hf _ h

/-- The set of all quasi-identities holding in `G` is a basis of quasi-identities of `G`. -/
@[category API, AMS 8 20]
theorem isBasisOf_setOf_holds (G : Type*) [Group G] :
    IsBasisOf {q : QuasiIdentity | q.Holds G} G :=
  ⟨fun _ hq => hq, fun q hq _ _ hH => hH q hq⟩

/-- The identity $x_0 = 1$, viewed as a quasi-identity without premises. -/
def trivialLaw : QuasiIdentity := ⟨∅, FreeGroup.of 0⟩

/-- The single identity $x_0 = 1$ is a basis of quasi-identities of the trivial group. -/
@[category test, AMS 8 20]
theorem isBasisOf_trivialLaw : IsBasisOf {trivialLaw} Unit := by
  refine ⟨fun q _ => holds_of_subsingleton q Unit, fun q _ H _ hH f _ => ?_⟩
  have h1 : ∀ h : H, h = 1 := fun h => by
    simpa [trivialLaw, Holds] using hH trivialLaw rfl (fun _ => h)
  exact h1 _

end QuasiIdentity

open QuasiIdentity

/--
Is it true that an independent basis of quasi-identities of any finite group is finite?

That is: for every finite group $G$ and every independent basis $B$ of the quasi-identities
of $G$, is $B$ finite?
-/
@[category research open, AMS 8 20]
theorem kourovka.«9.6» : answer(sorry) ↔
    ∀ (G : Type) [Group G] [Finite G] (B : Set QuasiIdentity),
      IsBasisOf B G → IsIndependent B → B.Finite := by
  sorry

end Kourovka.«9.6»

modeling_decisions: Quasi-identities are written in the form (w₁ = 1 ∧ … ∧ wₙ = 1) → w = 1 with group words wᵢ, w ∈ FreeGroup ℕ, rather than sᵢ = tᵢ → s = t. In groups these are interchangeable (s = t ⟺ s t⁻¹ = 1), and since independence forces the members of a basis to be pairwise non-equivalent, the finiteness of independent bases is invariant under any semantics-preserving change of representation.

Variables are indexed by ℕ (each word uses finitely many); satisfaction quantifies over all assignments ℕ → H, which is equivalent to quantifying over the finitely many occurring variables since groups are nonempty.

Premises form a Finset (so n = 0, i.e. identities, is allowed); this matches the usual definition (Mal'cev/Gorbunov) and does not affect the question since an identity is equivalent to a quasi-identity with a trivial premise.

Consequence is semantic and relative to the class of groups, with models H ranging over Type (universe 0), as elsewhere in the repository; by downward Löwenheim–Skolem this is equivalent to allowing models in any universe.
'Basis of quasi-identities of G' is formalized as: B ⊆ Q(G) and every quasi-identity of G is a consequence of B. This is equivalent to Mod(B) = quasivariety generated by G.
'Independent' is formalized as: no member of B is a consequence of B \ {member}. For a basis this is equivalent to 'no proper subset is a basis' (the phrasing in the decomposition note).
G ranges over all finite groups including the trivial group, following the source's 'any finite group'; no nontriviality hypothesis is added.

# Conjecture 9.6

by V. A. Gorbunov

Is it true that an independent basis of quasiidentities of any finite group is finite?

A *quasi-identity* in the signature of groups is a universal Horn sentence
$$\forall \bar x\ \bigl(t_1(\bar x) = s_1(\bar x) \wedge \dots \wedge t_k(\bar x) = s_k(\bar x)
\to t(\bar x) = s(\bar x)\bigr), \qquad k \ge 0,$$
where the $t_i, s_i, t, s$ are group words. The *quasi-identities of a group* $G$ are the
quasi-identities that hold in $G$. A set $B$ of quasi-identities is a *basis* of the
quasi-identities of $G$ if the groups satisfying $B$ are exactly the groups satisfying all
quasi-identities of $G$ (that is, $B$ axiomatizes the quasivariety generated by $G$), and $B$ is
*independent* if no member of $B$ is a consequence of the remaining members (equivalently, no
proper subset of $B$ is a basis).

Which finite groups have a *finite* basis of quasi-identities was settled by Ol'shanskii.
Problem 9.6 asks instead whether a finite group can have an infinite *independent* basis.

*Reference:* [The Kourovka Notebook](https://arxiv.org/abs/1401.0300v46)
-/

namespace Kourovka.«9.6»

/--
A quasi-identity in the signature of groups,
$$\forall \bar x\ \bigl(t_1 = s_1 \wedge \dots \wedge t_k = s_k \to t = s\bigr), \qquad k \ge 0.$$
The premises $t_i = s_i$ and the conclusion $t = s$ are equations between group words in the
variables $x_0, x_1, \dots$; a group word is represented by the element of the free group
`FreeGroup ℕ` it defines, since two words take the same value in every group under every
assignment of the variables exactly when they define the same element of the free group.
The case $k = 0$ is an identity.
-/
structure QuasiIdentity where
  /-- The premises $t_1 = s_1, \dots, t_k = s_k$, as pairs of words $(t_i, s_i)$. -/
  premises : Finset (FreeGroup ℕ × FreeGroup ℕ)
  /-- The conclusion $t = s$, as the pair of words $(t, s)$. -/
  conclusion : FreeGroup ℕ × FreeGroup ℕ

namespace QuasiIdentity

/--
The quasi-identity `q` holds in the group `H`: for every assignment `x : ℕ → H` of the
variables under which all premises $t_i(\bar x) = s_i(\bar x)$ hold, the conclusion
$t(\bar x) = s(\bar x)$ holds as well.
-/
def Holds (q : QuasiIdentity) (H : Type*) [Group H] : Prop :=
  ∀ x : ℕ → H, (∀ p ∈ q.premises, FreeGroup.lift x p.1 = FreeGroup.lift x p.2) →
    FreeGroup.lift x q.conclusion.1 = FreeGroup.lift x q.conclusion.2

/--
The quasi-identity `q` is a consequence of the set `B` of quasi-identities: every group in
which all members of `B` hold is a group in which `q` holds.
-/
def IsConsequence (B : Set QuasiIdentity) (q : QuasiIdentity) : Prop :=
  ∀ (H : Type) [Group H], (∀ p ∈ B, p.Holds H) → q.Holds H

/--
The set `B` is a basis of the quasi-identities of the group `G`: every member of `B` holds in
`G`, and every quasi-identity holding in `G` is a consequence of `B`. Equivalently, the groups
satisfying `B` are exactly the groups satisfying all quasi-identities of `G`, i.e. `B`
axiomatizes the quasivariety generated by `G`.
-/
def IsBasisOf (B : Set QuasiIdentity) (G : Type*) [Group G] : Prop :=
  (∀ q ∈ B, q.Holds G) ∧ ∀ q : QuasiIdentity, q.Holds G → IsConsequence B q

/--
The set `B` of quasi-identities is independent: no member of `B` is a consequence of the
remaining members. For a basis `B`, this says exactly that no proper subset of `B` is a basis.
-/
def Independent (B : Set QuasiIdentity) : Prop :=
  ∀ q ∈ B, ¬ IsConsequence (B \ {q}) q

/-- Every quasi-identity holds in the trivial group. -/
@[category test, AMS 8 20]
theorem holds_unit (q : QuasiIdentity) : q.Holds Unit :=
  fun _ _ ↦ Subsingleton.elim _ _

/-- The identity $x_0 x_1 = x_1 x_0$ holds in a group `H` if and only if `H` is commutative. -/

theorem holds_comm_iff (H : Type*) [Group H] :
    Holds ⟨∅, (FreeGroup.of 0 * FreeGroup.of 1, FreeGroup.of 1 * FreeGroup.of 0)⟩ H ↔
      Std.Commutative (α := H) (· * ·) := by
  constructor
  · intro h
    refine ⟨fun a b ↦ ?_⟩
    simpa using h (fun i ↦ if i = 0 then a else b) (by simp)
  · intro h x _
    simpa using h.comm (x 0) (x 1)

/-- The quasi-identity $x_0^2 = 1 \to x_0 = 1$ holds in `ℤ` (written multiplicatively). -/
@[category test, AMS 8 20]
theorem holds_multiplicative_int :
    Holds ⟨{(FreeGroup.of 0 ^ 2, 1)}, (FreeGroup.of 0, 1)⟩ (Multiplicative ℤ) := by
  intro x h
  have := h _ (Finset.mem_singleton_self _)
  simp only [map_pow, FreeGroup.lift_apply_of, map_one] at this ⊢
  exact (pow_eq_one_iff_left two_ne_zero).mp this

/-- The quasi-identity $x_0^2 = 1 \to x_0 = 1$ fails in the group of order two. -/

theorem not_holds_multiplicative_zmod_two :
    ¬ Holds ⟨{(FreeGroup.of 0 ^ 2, 1)}, (FreeGroup.of 0, 1)⟩ (Multiplicative (ZMod 2)) := by
  intro h
  have := h (fun _ ↦ Multiplicative.ofAdd 1) (by decide)
  simp at this

end QuasiIdentity

That is: for every finite group $G$ and every independent basis $B$ of the quasi-identities
of $G$, is $B$ finite?
-/

/-- A quasi-identity in the group signature: a finite conjunction of equations
between group words in finitely many variables implies another such equation. -/
structure GroupQuasiIdentity where
  /-- The number of variables. -/
  numVariables : ℕ
  /-- The equations in the antecedent. -/
  hypotheses : List (FreeGroup (Fin numVariables) × FreeGroup (Fin numVariables))
  /-- The equation in the consequent. -/
  conclusion : FreeGroup (Fin numVariables) × FreeGroup (Fin numVariables)

/-- A group satisfies a quasi-identity if the implication holds under every
assignment of its variables. -/
def GroupQuasiIdentity.Holds (q : GroupQuasiIdentity) (G : Type*) [Group G] : Prop :=
  ∀ valuation : Fin q.numVariables → G,
    (∀ equation ∈ q.hypotheses,
      FreeGroup.lift valuation equation.1 = FreeGroup.lift valuation equation.2) →
    FreeGroup.lift valuation q.conclusion.1 = FreeGroup.lift valuation q.conclusion.2

/-- A set of group quasi-identities is a basis for the quasi-identities of `G`
if its group models are exactly the groups satisfying every quasi-identity
valid in `G`. -/
def IsBasisFor (G : Type*) [Group G] (B : Set GroupQuasiIdentity) : Prop :=
  ∀ (H : Type) [Group H],
    (∀ q ∈ B, q.Holds H) ↔ ∀ q : GroupQuasiIdentity, q.Holds G → q.Holds H

/-- An independent basis is a basis no proper subset of which is still a basis. -/
def IsIndependentBasisFor (G : Type*) [Group G] (B : Set GroupQuasiIdentity) : Prop :=
  IsBasisFor G B ∧ ∀ B' ⊂ B, ¬IsBasisFor G B'

Is it true that every independent basis of quasi-identities of every finite
group is finite?

Here a basis axiomatizes, among groups, the quasivariety generated by the given
group, and independence means that no proper subset is also such a basis.
-/

    ∀ (G : Type) [Group G] [Finite G] (B : Set GroupQuasiIdentity),

  sorry

end Kourovka.«9.6»

import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Conjecture 9.6

by V. A. Gorbunov

Is it true that an independent basis of quasiidentities of any finite group is finite?

A quasi-identity in the language of groups is a universal Horn sentence
$$\forall x_0 \dots x_n \; (t_1 = s_1 \wedge \dots \wedge t_k = s_k \to t = s),$$
where $t_i, s_i, t, s$ are group words in the variables $x_0, \dots, x_n$. Identities
are the quasi-identities with $k = 0$. A group $H$ satisfies a quasi-identity if it holds
for every assignment of the variables in $H$.

A *basis of quasi-identities* of a group $G$ is a set $B$ of quasi-identities of $G$ such
that every quasi-identity of $G$ is a consequence of $B$ in the class of all groups, i.e.
$B$ axiomatizes (modulo the group axioms) the quasivariety generated by $G$. The basis $B$
is *independent* if no member of $B$ is a consequence of the remaining members of $B$;
equivalently, no proper subset of $B$ is a basis.

The question is not whether every finite group has a finite basis of quasi-identities
(by a theorem of A. Yu. Ol'shanskii this holds exactly when all Sylow subgroups are
abelian), but whether an independent basis of quasi-identities of a finite group is
necessarily finite.

*Reference:* [The Kourovka Notebook](https://arxiv.org/abs/1401.0300v46)
-/

namespace Kourovka.«9.6»

/-- A quasi-identity in the language of groups: a finite list of premises $t_i = s_i$ and
a conclusion $t = s$, where all terms are group words in the variables $x_0, x_1, \dots$,
represented as elements of the free group `FreeGroup ℕ`. It stands for the universal Horn
sentence $\forall \bar x \; (\bigwedge_i t_i = s_i \to t = s)$. An identity is a
quasi-identity with no premises. -/
structure QuasiIdentity where
  /-- The premises $t_1 = s_1, \dots, t_k = s_k$. -/
  premises : List (FreeGroup ℕ × FreeGroup ℕ)
  /-- The conclusion $t = s$. -/
  conclusion : FreeGroup ℕ × FreeGroup ℕ

/-- A group `H` satisfies the quasi-identity `q` if for every assignment
`f : ℕ → H` of the variables under which all premises of `q` hold, the conclusion of `q`
holds as well. -/
def QuasiIdentity.Holds (q : QuasiIdentity) (H : Type*) [Group H] : Prop :=
  ∀ f : ℕ → H, (∀ p ∈ q.premises, FreeGroup.lift f p.1 = FreeGroup.lift f p.2) →
    FreeGroup.lift f q.conclusion.1 = FreeGroup.lift f q.conclusion.2

/-- A quasi-identity `q` is a consequence of a set `B` of quasi-identities if every group
satisfying all members of `B` satisfies `q`. -/
def Consequence (B : Set QuasiIdentity) (q : QuasiIdentity) : Prop :=
  ∀ (H : Type) [Group H], (∀ b ∈ B, b.Holds H) → q.Holds H

/-- A set `B` of quasi-identities is a basis of quasi-identities of the group `G` if every
member of `B` holds in `G` and every quasi-identity holding in `G` is a consequence of `B`.
Equivalently, the groups satisfying `B` are exactly the groups in the quasivariety generated
by `G`. -/
def IsBasis (G : Type*) [Group G] (B : Set QuasiIdentity) : Prop :=
  (∀ b ∈ B, b.Holds G) ∧ ∀ q : QuasiIdentity, q.Holds G → Consequence B q

/-- A set `B` of quasi-identities is independent if no member of `B` is a consequence of
the remaining members of `B`. -/
def IsIndependent (B : Set QuasiIdentity) : Prop :=
  ∀ b ∈ B, ¬ Consequence (B \ {b}) b

/-- Every quasi-identity holds in a trivial group. -/
@[category API, AMS 3 20]
theorem QuasiIdentity.holds_of_subsingleton (q : QuasiIdentity) (H : Type*) [Group H]
    [Subsingleton H] : q.Holds H :=
  fun _ _ => Subsingleton.elim _ _

/-- The set of all quasi-identities of a group `G` is a basis of quasi-identities of `G`. -/
@[category API, AMS 3 20]
theorem isBasis_setOf_holds (G : Type*) [Group G] : IsBasis G {q | q.Holds G} :=
  ⟨fun _ hq => hq, fun q hq _ _ hB => hB q hq⟩

/--
Is it true that an independent basis of quasi-identities of any finite group is finite?

That is, for every finite group $G$ and every independent basis $B$ of quasi-identities of
$G$, is $B$ finite?
-/
@[category research open, AMS 3 20]
theorem kourovka.«9.6» : answer(sorry) ↔
    ∀ (G : Type) [Group G] [Finite G] (B : Set QuasiIdentity),
      IsBasis G B → IsIndependent B → B.Finite := by
  sorry

end Kourovka.«9.6»
